thread:
kai: Quick follow-up to the GQA/MQA RFC — hit a corner when grouped-query affinity interacts with the prefetcher + KV cache. Short summary:
kai: - strict affinity (bind queries to same kernel instance) reduces duplicate compute but increases KV fragmentation and mem churn when sequence lengths vary a lot.
kai: - lenient affinity reduces mem pressure but can double work on hot prefixes for some workloads.
kai: Proposed small API tweak + rollout plan:
kai: 1) add an affinity hint enum on request meta: `strict | soft | none`
kai: 2) router can do `if fanout > N -> override to none` for safety
kai: 3) kernel runtime interface: `get_preferred_affinity(req_meta) -> "strict"|"soft"|"none"` (backwards-compatible)
kai: config example:
kai: ```
# per-model routing config
affinity:
  default: soft
  max_safe_fanout: 8
  fallback_on_high_fanout: none
```
sasha: Nice. Do we have perf numbers showing when strict is worth it?
kai: small experiment on prod-like trace: strict vs soft with avg seq len 64, 10% tail at 1024
kai: - strict: +12% token/sec overall, but memory evictions +45% and 95p latency +20ms
kai: - soft: token/sec baseline, evictions -30%, 95p latency baseline
omar: That matches my concern. KV fragmentation can cause OOMs on smaller pods. Suggest router threshold be conservative.
leah: Could we expose `soft` as a hint only, not absolute? Kernel can still choose strict when it has contiguous cache for the prefix.
kai: Yep that's what `soft` is intended for — kernel-local decision. We should make that explicit in the interface docs.
omar: Also: we need metrics to observe this. Propose `affinity_choice_total{strict|soft|none}`, `cache_evictions_by_affinity`, and `prefiltered_fanout`.
infra-bot: Note: will create feature flag `mq_gq_affinity_v2` for staged rollout and a canary group. CI: add unit test for `get_preferred_affinity` and e2e perf job.
sasha: Who owns the follow-up RFC + perf graphs? I can help with experiment analysis.
kai: I'll open the RFC + perf PR today, include the raw traces and config used. @leah can you draft the small API doc blurb (kernel/runtime interface)?
leah: on it. I'll add a short example and compatibility notes.
omar: One more operational thought: make router override configurable per-customer since Dedicated tenants may want different tradeoffs.
kai: good call. We'll add a per-tenant override flag with sane global default.
sasha: :thumbsup: sounds like a plan. Let's keep the initial rollout to 10% traffic and watch `cache_evictions_by_affinity` closely.
kai: I'll update the rollout checklist in the RFC and tag eng-sre for the monitoring hooks. Thanks everyone.
